experiment_description: Base config for paper pairwise cross-family runs. The one-click script runs one model and one family pair per output directory.

interface_exposure.explanation: Interface exposure perturbs names, aliases, descriptions, and separability. Parameter errors may appear downstream as spillover, but direct schema-level changes are out of bounds.

user_intent.explanation: User-intent perturbations directly distort request interpretation. Parameter mistakes are allowed as downstream spillover, but registry or environment mutations are disallowed direct effects.

observation.explanation: Observation perturbations directly affect returned data and execution handling. A downstream no-call can be cascade, but request rewriting or interface-surface mutation is out of bounds.

execution_environment.explanation: Execution-environment perturbations directly affect runtime behavior and error surfaces. Wrong-parameter may appear as spillover, but request or interface mutations are disallowed direct effects.

S1 Tool Selection.explanation: S1 captures the earliest selection failure. Parameter mistakes can still show up later as spillover after a confused selection path.

S2 Interface Grounding.explanation: S2 covers interface grounding and description understanding. Wrong-tool and parameter-binding mistakes can both surface here, while no-call is treated as spillover from unresolved grounding.

S3 Parameter Binding.explanation: S3 is the binding stage. Invalid-format may appear as spillover when parameter binding destabilizes the emitted call.

S4 Observation / Execution Handling.explanation: S4 captures observation/execution handling. A no-call can still be a cascade when the model gives up after unstable execution feedback.
